rootCause: Xenon hosts Alloy-style browsers in native child windows. CEF attaches no Chrome theme to those WebContents, so Chromium derives prefers-color-scheme from the process-wide NativeTheme (the Windows app mode). CefRequestContext::SetChromeColorScheme changes only the profile ThemeService, which Chrome-style Views surfaces read.

checks.coverage: Full production and authentication-fixture build; 11 native groups; adapter, login-capture, human-autofill, protected-login and form-fill node suites (22, 32, 31, 10 and 6 tests); 5 branding checks

observations: Theme Light: fixture reported light; fixture canvas and about:blank painted rgb(255,255,255)
Theme Dark: fixture reported dark; fixture canvas and about:blank painted rgb(18,18,18)
Theme System: fixture reported dark and about:blank painted rgb(18,18,18); native Theme: Light command saved light; pages opened before and after the switch kept dark
Restart after the runtime switch: fixture reported light; fixture canvas and about:blank painted rgb(255,255,255)

checks.note: Not run yet: the suite never changes the Windows app mode. Theme Dark is the discriminating case in this mode.

checks.command: node tests/theme-integration.mjs (baseline copy targeting the unfixed binary)
checks.observation: Reproduces the report: with Theme Light saved under Windows dark mode, the fixture reported prefers-color-scheme dark

limitations: The theme menu is driven by native WM_COMMAND messages to the fixture's own shell window, not physical menu input.

Chromium reads force-light-mode and force-dark-mode once per process, so a runtime theme change reaches web content only after restart. A live update would need a per-page protocol override, which Xenon does not use for colors.
A Windows app-mode change while Xenon runs with Theme System was not exercised; the suite reads the Windows mode and never changes it.

The baseline binary was a snapshot of a concurrent local build of unrelated, uncommitted shell work with the same theme code as this change's base commit; it serves only to show the suite detects the reported failure.
Fixtures are synthetic loopback pages; no real website was loaded.
